question: Why do twisted tolane derivatives exhibit phosphorescence in glassy media at low temperature while planar ones do not?
answer: Twisted tolane derivatives exhibit phosphorescence in glassy media at low temperatures due to their ability to overcome an energy barrier in the excited S₁ state, populating a trans-bent minimum (¹¹Aᵤ state) with sufficient excess energy. This state facilitates intersystem crossing (ISC) into the triplet (¹³B₂ᵤ) state, enabling phosphorescence. In contrast, planar derivatives lack the excess energy to surmount the barrier, remaining in the planar S₁ₚ minimum (¹¹B₂ᵤ state) and emitting only fluorescence. The rigidity of the glassy matrix at low temperatures further stabilizes the long-lived triplet state, allowing phosphorescence to occur exclusively in twisted derivatives.

It aims to explain how the molecular structure, temperature, and external conditions influence absorption and fluorescence spectra, fluorescence quantum yield, and the occurrence of phosphorescence in specific conditions.
